title: Deferred sparse edit capacity and channel-local promotion
scope: Synthetic Tedd.Voxtree 32³ chunk workloads on one AVX2 x64 host. The investigation covers 1–20-write priority cases, capacity overflow, channel locality, storage acquisition, lookup structure, repackaging, and explicit MakeHot behavior.
question: Can small voxel edits remain outside the compressed octree, and can overflow materialize only affected channels without regressing the common sparse path?

summary.headline: Channel-local promotion reduced the source-matched capacity-256 terrain overflow edit median by 90.6%; ordinary 20-write medians changed by less than 1%.

hypotheses.claim: A lower default capacity reduces pooled storage and cache cost for one to twenty writes.
hypotheses.mechanism: Use a smaller ArrayPool bucket and promote earlier.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 10% faster or 4× less payload with under 5% time regression.
hypotheses.result: Capacities 32–256 showed no stable low-count advantage; capacity 20 made write 21 trigger a 132–364 µs full expansion. Retained pool memory was not measured.

hypotheses.claim: Overflow can materialize affected channels independently.
hypotheses.mechanism: Preserve encoded untouched channels and compact residual sparse keys.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 50% faster for one-of-eight overflow with under 5% ordinary-path regression.
hypotheses.result: Against exact f9d9b36, one-channel overflow edit medians improved 90.6–97.9%; complete cycles improved 68.3–90.1%; serialization improved 67.6–90.1%. Ordinary 20-write medians changed -0.12% and -0.67%.

hypotheses.claim: Channel-local promotion makes capacity 32 a superior default.
hypotheses.mechanism: Bound quadratic search by promoting at 33 positions.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 10% weighted gain without a priority regression over 5%.
hypotheses.result: No smaller tested capacity established a superior default; earlier promotion increases dense-work exposure. The optimal threshold remains workload-dependent.

hypotheses.claim: A last-key cache accelerates repeated writes.
hypotheses.mechanism: Bypass lookup when consecutive keys match.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 10% repeated-write gain with under 2% distinct-write regression.
hypotheses.result: Repeated-versus-distinct workloads do not isolate a last-key cache implementation.

hypotheses.claim: A hybrid index outperforms vectorized search at high occupancy.
hypotheses.mechanism: Replace cumulative linear insertion probes with expected constant-time lookup.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 20% faster at 256 or more positions including maintenance.
hypotheses.result: A Dictionary kernel established a crossover but excluded integrated allocation and maintenance; H-022 tested one integrated form.

hypotheses.claim: A caller-owned typed provider reduces acquisition cost or retained memory.
hypotheses.mechanism: Reuse heterogeneous buffers with shared-pool fallback.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 10% caller gain or materially improved memory behavior.
hypotheses.result: An integrated reusable typed-pool prototype changed the median by -9.23% for uniform data and +0.40% for terrain data, allocated the same 224 B, and failed the 10% threshold across patterns.
hypotheses.decision: Reject as a speed API; deterministic-memory utility remains unmeasured

hypotheses.claim: Allocating exact arrays per short-lived edit session outperforms shared pooling.
hypotheses.mechanism: Avoid rent/return and bucket inflation.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 10% faster acquisition with acceptable GC cost.
hypotheses.result: Exact allocation cost 58.978 ns and 1,672 B at capacity 256 versus 42.705–53.039 ns and zero managed allocation for warm pooling.

hypotheses.claim: Channel-specific edit counts reduce sparse application work.
hypotheses.mechanism: Iterate only values present in a channel.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 10% faster in sparse-per-channel publication.
hypotheses.result: Channel-local promotion removed the dominant cost before this secondary representation change was justified.

hypotheses.claim: Handwritten SIMD improves key lookup over Span.IndexOf.
hypotheses.mechanism: Use explicit vector comparisons and masks.
hypotheses.prediction: Integrated caller improvement without portability regression.
hypotheses.result: .NET 10 already emitted AVX2 vpcmpeqw/vptest; prior explicit SIMD regressed integrated workloads.

hypotheses.claim: A startup-frozen deferred-write flag removes meaningful branch cost.
hypotheses.mechanism: Replace the per-instance option branch with an AppContext switch.
hypotheses.prediction: Repeatable gain beyond the 5% noise threshold.
hypotheses.result: Measured effects ranged from -2.8% to +0.5%, inside the threshold.

hypotheses.claim: Caller-supplied or retained repackage scratch improves publication.
hypotheses.mechanism: Eliminate one shared-pool acquisition per call.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 10% faster complete cycles.
hypotheses.result: The measured acquisition ceiling is below 0.4% of the shortest complete cycle.

hypotheses.claim: Geometric physical growth reduces first-write storage without harming time.
hypotheses.mechanism: Rent 32 slots initially and double to the logical capacity.
hypotheses.prediction: Under 5% priority-path regression.
hypotheses.result: 32-entry workloads regressed 13.3–15.1%; 64-entry workloads regressed 47.5–53.5%.

hypotheses.claim: AVX2 batched probes amortize key-vector loads for clustered requests.
hypotheses.mechanism: Compare each loaded key vector with several broadcast query keys.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 20% faster for batches of 8–32 at 64–256 entries.
hypotheses.result: The public API is scalar and Span.IndexOf already emits AVX2 comparisons.

hypotheses.claim: Presence-bitmask enumeration accelerates sparse application.
hypotheses.mechanism: Enumerate set bits with trailing-zero count instead of scanning all keys.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 10% faster below 25% per-channel occupancy.
hypotheses.result: No representative low-occupancy-per-channel publication trace was available.

hypotheses.claim: Block-copying partial channels accelerates explicit MakeHot.
hypotheses.mechanism: Copy materialized spans and decode only encoded channels.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 10% faster per materialized channel.
hypotheses.result: Source-matched complete MakeHot medians ranged from 10.1% faster to 13.4% slower. The block copy remains a necessary H-002 detail but gave no consistent complete-path gain.

hypotheses.claim: Software prefetch reduces encoded-channel decode stalls.
hypotheses.mechanism: Prefetch cache lines ahead of the sequential decoder.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 10% faster terrain materialization.
hypotheses.result: The measured decoder is sequential and warm-cache; no cold-stream trace justified target-specific intrinsics.

hypotheses.claim: A direct position map beats linear search at high occupancy.
hypotheses.mechanism: Index sparse slots by packed voxel position with generations or a bitmask.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 25% faster above crossover while remaining smaller than one dense channel.
hypotheses.result: A 32³ map costs 64–128 KiB plus metadata; the 64 KiB form remains below one 128 KiB uint dense channel, so static accounting does not falsify the speed claim.

hypotheses.claim: Cache-line grouped overlay blocks improve locality.
hypotheses.mechanism: Group keys, presence summaries, and common values while retaining vector key lanes.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 10% faster at 64–256 positions with under 25% payload growth.
hypotheses.result: No measured locality attribution justified replacing the vector-searchable structure-of-arrays layout.

hypotheses.claim: False-sharing-resistant scheduling improves concurrent store throughput.
hypotheses.mechanism: Shard or pad independently mutated pending metadata.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 15% throughput or p99 improvement under contention.
hypotheses.result: DeferredOctreeChunk is exclusively owned; the synchronized store needs a separate contention investigation.

hypotheses.claim: Stencil-aware Morton runs compress and apply coherent edits efficiently.
hypotheses.mechanism: Coalesce identical adjacent Morton operations into runs and fill or block-copy them.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 20% faster or half the payload for 3×3×3 and planar stencils.
hypotheses.result: No representative stencil trace or batch-write API was available.

hypotheses.claim: An adaptive threshold based on channel count and decode cost beats a fixed capacity.
hypotheses.mechanism: Promote when estimated sparse cost exceeds one channel decode.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 10% weighted gain without a priority regression over 5%.
hypotheses.result: No application distribution supplied defensible weights; source variability risks unstable behavior.
hypotheses.decision: Retain fixed threshold; optimal capacity remains workload-dependent

hypotheses.claim: A pooled open-addressed index above a threshold removes quadratic insertion growth.
hypotheses.mechanism: Build a compact hash table after 256–512 entries.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 30% faster at 1,024–4,096 writes with under 2% regression below 256.
hypotheses.result: The prototype improved 1,024–4,096 writes by about 70–87%. Effects across 20–64 writes ranged from a 15.1% improvement to a 36.0% regression and allocation rose, violating the 2% guard.

retainedChanges: Sparse overflow promotes the channel that frees the most exclusive keys into a pooled dense Morton buffer.
Residual shared-position edits remain sparse; untouched channel encodings remain immutable and shared.
Repackage encodes only dense or sparsely changed channels and reuses unchanged encoded channel memory.
Explicit MakeHot combines partial dense channels, residual sparse edits, and still-encoded channels into full hot storage.
The default capacity remains 256, physical sparse buffers remain fixed-capacity shared-pool rentals, and deferred writes remain enabled by default.
decisions: Retain 256 as the conservative default because no smaller tested capacity established a superior threshold; the optimal capacity remains workload-dependent.
Keep fixed shared-pool buffers. The integrated caller-provider prototype failed the 10% speed threshold across uniform and terrain inputs; deterministic-memory utility was not measured.
Do not add handwritten SIMD, geometric growth, or the tested pooled hash index. Last-key caching and a direct voxel map remain inconclusive.
A caller-supplied workspace remains a possible deterministic-memory feature; no measured speed case justifies it.
Treat explicit MakeHot as a full-expansion operation; channel-local optimization targets edits, publication, and serialization before that request.
correctness: Release tests passed: 320 on net8.0, 321 on net10.0, and 322 on net11.0.
Tests cover partial promotion, residual sparse edits, repeated overflow epochs, explicit zero, overwrites, wide keys, generic bit fidelity, disposal, and snapshot immutability.
Tests verify untouched encoded channels retain memory identity after channel-local publication.
Tests verify explicit MakeHot applies all partial and sparse state before returning borrowed dense storage.

generatedCode.summary: The retained Span<ushort>.IndexOf lookup uses AVX2 vector comparison on .NET 10.
generatedCode.before: No scalar-only deficiency was observed in the retained implementation.
generatedCode.after: Generated code contains vpcmpeqw and vptest; explicit SIMD therefore duplicates runtime specialization.

validityThreats: No Forcecraft application trace supplied the distribution of distinct positions, repeated writes, touched channels, or publication cadence.
Benchmarks are synthetic library workloads on one Ryzen 9 5950X host; ARM64, AVX-512, server GC, and other runtimes were not measured.
ArrayPool retained process memory is not represented by BenchmarkDotNet managed-allocation counters.
Overflow comparisons used ShortRun with three retained measurements; ordinary-path and provider comparisons used MediumRun.
No exclusive CPU profile supplied defensible hotspot percentages; the report therefore does not fabricate an Amdahl attribution.
Explicit MakeHot necessarily expands all channels and ranged from 10.1% faster to 13.4% slower across measured cases.
reproduction: Use run-source-matched-benchmarks.ps1 with separate baseline and candidate worktree paths.
The script requires the baseline at f9d9b366ede89050800bc97df9fca2a086ab1ce2, verifies candidate src/ against product revision 4006838, and verifies identical benchmark fixtures.
Each dotnet invocation acquires D:\Temp\BenchmarkLock.txt through run-exclusive-benchmark.ps1.
The script executes the MediumRun 20-write priority filter and the ShortRun capacity-overflow filters for both worktrees.
Run normalize-results.py against each paired artifact directory, then render report-data.json with the scientific-method-performance render_report.py script.
